name: London Sweep Reversal
hypothesis: During the London open (07:00-09:00 UTC bar closes), stops resting beyond the Asian session range (00:00-06:00 UTC) are swept and price closes back inside the range; the subsequent rotation toward the opposite Asian boundary offers asymmetric payoff with the sweep extreme as structural invalidation.
entry_conditions: M15 bar closing 07:00-09:00 UTC whose low undercuts the Asian low by at least 0.05 ATR(14) and closes back above it in the upper half of its range (LONG), symmetric for SHORT; Asian range built from at least 20 M15 bars and not wider than 4 ATR; no earlier sweep of either Asian boundary earlier the same day; planned RR >= 2.
exit_conditions: Fixed stop-loss and take-profit; take-profit at the opposite Asian session boundary; time exit after 18 hours if neither barrier trades.
stop_loss_method: Sweep bar extreme minus/plus 0.15 M15 ATR(14) buffer; risk must be between 0.6 and 5 ATR.
take_profit_method: Opposite Asian range boundary (structural liquidity objective); trade admitted only when (target-entry)/risk >= 2.
risk_model: One planned risk unit per opportunity; one opportunity per symbol per day enforced by model state; per-symbol overlap lock enforced by the common evaluator.
intended_conditions: FX majors, gold and crypto during liquid London hours; regimes where session liquidity pools get swept and retrace (mean-rotating intraday regimes).
limitations: UTC-fixed windows ignore daylight-saving shifts; excludes indices (shared evaluator cannot finance modes 2/3); spread/risk gate 0.1 not always met on wide-spread symbols; small sample sizes per symbol; historical partitions already exposed to prior research.
